scenes.say: WebSockets or Server-Sent Events—which lets you send data both ways in real time?

scenes.label: WebSocket
scenes.sub: Full-duplex, persistent connection for real-time data.
scenes.say: WebSockets create a full-duplex, persistent connection. That means real-time data flows both ways—client and server.

scenes.label: SSE
scenes.sub: Server pushes updates to browser, one-way only.
scenes.say: Server-Sent Events, or SSE, let the server push updates to the browser. But it's one-way—server to client only.
WebSockets are bidirectional, perfect for chat apps. SSE is for simple live feeds—just server to client.

scenes.question: Can SSE send data from client to server?
scenes.right: No—SSE only pushes from server to client.
scenes.say: Here's a common trap: Can SSE send data from client to server? No—SSE only pushes from server to client.
